content.identity:
Samuel A. Cohen is a long-tenured Principal Research Physicist at the Princeton Plasma Physics Laboratory (PPPL), operating under Princeton University's School of Engineering and Applied Science and the U.S. Department of Energy (DOE). His institutional email at the lab is **scohen@pppl.gov**. PPPL's primary profile catalog displays him under "Sam Cohen" with the line "Sam Cohen, Title: Principal Research Physicist, Email: scohen@pppl.gov, PPPL Logo, Princeton Plasma Physics Laboratory, 100 Stellarator Road, Princeton, NJ" [identity[0]] [10]. Email: scohen@pppl.gov" [identity[1]] [1]. The Princeton Materials Institute directory describes him as "Director, Program in Plasma Science and Technology, P.I., Magnetic Nozzle & FRC Experiments. Lecturer with the rank of Professor in Astrophysical Sciences" [identity[2]] [73]. The PPPL-hosted CV page confirms: "Director, Program in Plasma Physics and Technology, Princeton University. Principal Investigator, Magnetic Nozzle and FRC Experiments, Plasma Science and Technology Department, PPPL. Ph.D., Massachusetts Institute of Technology, 1973" [identity[3]] [74]. He earned a B.S. in Physics at MIT in 1968 and Ph.D. at MIT in 1973, with research interests in Magnetic Fusion, Field-Reversed Configuration, Dynamic Stabilization, Advanced (Aneutronic) Fuels for Fusion, Plasma Thrusters for Space Propulsion, Plasma Recombination, and Nonlinear Dynamics of Charged Particles in FRCs [identity[2]] [73].

His lead programs are the **Princeton Field-Reversed Configuration (PFRC)**, including the **PFRC-2** device, and fusion-propulsion thrusters (PFRC rocket concept).
